extracted.intended_audience: patent examiners and patent owners (and their attorneys/agents) involved in ex parte reexamination proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules governing responses, amendments, appeals, briefs, examiner actions, interviews, and disclosure duties in ex parte reexamination proceedings (MPEP guidance).

rubrics_metrics.name: Time for response to final rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: The statutory period for response to a final rejection in a reexamination proceeding will normally be two (2) months. The time period is automatically extended by 1 month if the response is the first response after the final rejection and a notice of appeal has not yet been filed; any timely first response (even informal or unsigned) automatically results in the extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advisory Office action using form PTOL-467 will inform the patent owner of the automatic 1 month extension. The period for response may not be extended to run past 6 months from the date of the final rejection. Notification of the examiner’s ruling should reach the patent owner with sufficient time to consider and act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments after final rejection — general rule
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent owner cannot, as a matter of right, amend any finally rejected claims, add new claims after a final rejection, or reinstate previously canceled claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For an amendment filed after final rejection and prior to the appeal brief, a showing under 37 CFR 1.116(b) is required and will be evaluated by the examiner for all proposed amendments after final rejection except where amendment merely cancels claims, adopts examiner’s suggestions, removes issues for appeal, or requires only cursory review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for entry of an amendment after final rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment filed after final rejection but before an appeal brief may be entered upon or after filing of an appeal provided certain conditions are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entry permitted if (A) total effect is to cancel claims or comply with a formal requirement previously set forth, or present rejected claims in better form for consideration on appeal; or (B) for an amendment touching the merits, the patent owner provides a showing of good and sufficient reasons why the amendment is necessary and was not earlier presented. The first proposed amendment after final action will be given sufficient consideration to determine patentability or reduction/simplification of appeal issues. Unless entered in entirety, examiner will briefly explain reasons for not entering; identify new issues requiring search and explain why; notify if portions would be entered if filed separately. Any second or subsequent amendment after final will be considered only to the extent it removes issues for appeal or puts a claim in obvious patentable condition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner handling of omissions or informal/defective responses after final
rubrics_metrics.description: The practice of giving a time period to supply an omission (MPEP § 2266.01) or notifying defects via PTOL-475 (MPEP § 2266.02) does not apply after a final Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a bona fide response filed after final rejection omits a point necessary to fully respond, the examiner should not issue a notice of failure to fully respond but should issue an advisory Office action (form PTOL-467) explaining the omission. If a defective (informal) response is filed after final, the examiner should not issue PTOL-475 but should issue PTOL-467 with an explanation of the defect (informality).

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to appeal in ex parte reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner involved in a reexamination proceeding may appeal under 35 U.S.C. 134 and seek court review under 35 U.S.C. 141–145 with respect to any decision adverse to patentability of any original or proposed amended or new claim. A third party requester may not appeal or participate in the patent owner’s appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For proceedings filed before Nov 29, 1999, appeal may be taken after the second rejection (final or non-final); for proceedings filed on/after Nov 29, 1999, appeal only after final rejection. The notice of appeal need not be signed; the fee required by 37 CFR 41.20(b)(1) must accompany the notice. Normal ex parte appeal procedures (37 CFR 41.31–41.54) apply in ex parte reexamination except as noted in the Chapter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing period and effect of first response on notice of appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: The period for filing the notice of appeal is the period set for response in the last Office action (normally 2 months). The timely filing of a first response to a final rejection with a shortened statutory period is construed as including a request to extend the period for response an additional month, as long as the period does not exceed 6 months from the date of the final rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the patent owner does not timely file a notice of appeal and/or fee, the appeal will be dismissed and form PTOL-468 will be used; prosecution is terminated and a Notice of Intent to Issue Ex Parte Reexamination Certificate (NIRC) will be issued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defective notice of appeal — cure period
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a notice of appeal is defective, the patent owner will be notified using form PTOL-475 and provided a time period to cure the defect(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 'other' box on PTOL-475 will be checked where appropriate with an explanation. A 1-month or 30 days (whichever is longer) time period will be provided to cure defects in the appeal notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments and appeal briefs — prohibition on including amendments in brief
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the appeal brief is not filed, but within the period allowed for filing the brief an amendment is presented which places the claims in patentable condition, the amendment may be entered. Amendments should not be included in the appeal brief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate amendments (not included with the brief) filed with or after the appeal are governed by MPEP § 1207.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time for filing appeal brief
rubrics_metrics.description: The time for filing the appeal brief is 2 months from the date of the appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent owners must meet this deadline or seek permitted extensions (see next metric).

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of time for filing appeal brief
rubrics_metrics.description: If unable to file a brief in time, the patent owner may file a petition with the appropriate extension of time fee to the Technology Center requesting additional time (usually 1 month).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If sufficient cause shown and petition filed prior to expiration, TC Director authorized to grant up to 1 month. Requests for more than 1 month will not be granted unless extraordinary circumstances (e.g., death, incapacitation). Time extended is added to the last calendar day of the original period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure to timely file appeal brief or fee
rubrics_metrics.description: Failure to file the brief and/or the appeal brief fee within the permissible time will result in dismissal of the appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form PTOL-468 is used to notify dismissal. Reexamination prosecution is terminated and an NIRC will subsequently be issued indicating status of claims at time of appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for the appeal brief content and form
rubrics_metrics.description: A fee per 37 CFR 41.20(b)(2) is required for filing the appeal brief. 37 CFR 41.37 requires the appellant to file a brief of authorities and arguments relied on, including a summary of claimed subject matter which must refer to the specification by page and line number, to drawings by reference characters, and a copy of the claims involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only one copy of the appeal brief is required. Where a third party requester filed the reexamination request, a copy of the brief must be served on that requester. In merged proceedings, one original copy of the brief should be provided for each reexamination proceeding and reissue application in the merged proceeding, and served on any third party requesters. The copy of claims should be double spaced, start on a new page, and include all underlining and bracketing reflecting changes; new claims added should be completely underlined (departure from MPEP §1205.02 for applications).

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsiveness of brief to all grounds of rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Briefs in appeal cases must be responsive to every ground of rejection stated by the examiner so that no search of the record is required to determine the appellant's position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The fact that appellant considers a ground clearly improper does not justify failure to point out reasons in the brief. A reply brief, if filed, shall be entered, except amendments or affidavits/evidence are subject to 37 CFR 1.116 and 41.33. See 37 CFR 41.41(a)(2). Failure to traverse every ground may lead to summary sustainment of that ground.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defective appeal brief — examiner notification and cure
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an appeal brief is defective, the examiner will notify the patent owner that the brief is defective using PTOL-462R and provide a 1-month period to cure the defect(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If items 1–9 on the form do not cover the defect, box 10 should be checked and the nature of defect(s) explained in an attachment. Example: inadvertent failure to respond to a ground—appellant gets 1 month to file a supplemental brief. Examiner must identify defects and give 1 month; failure to follow this may cause Board to return file for compliance. Intentional failure to respond should be noted to the Board and may lead to summary sustainment; oral argument will not remedy such deficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency of arguments vs absence of arguments in brief
rubrics_metrics.description: A distinction exists between the lack of any argument and presentation of arguments that carry no conviction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If brief lacks any argument on a ground, summarily sustaining the rejection is in order. If weak arguments are presented, a decision on the merits is made (though it may be an affirmance based on examiner grounds). Filing any paper titled as a brief is not necessarily compliance with 37 CFR 41.37; the rule requires setting forth authorities and arguments relied on.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner’s answer — content and determination of appealability
rubrics_metrics.description: The primary examiner may furnish a written answer to the appeal brief including explanations of the invention, references relied upon, and grounds of rejection, supplying a copy to appellant. If the examiner determines the appeal does not comply with 41.31/41.37 or is not appealable, the examiner shall make such determination of record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 41.39(a). MPEP §1207–1207.05 relate to preparation of examiner’s answers; these procedures apply to appeals in both applications and reexamination proceedings except as provided in this Chapter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner’s answer containing a new ground of rejection — appellant options
rubrics_metrics.description: If examiner’s answer contains a rejection designated as a new ground of rejection, appellant must within two months either: (1) request reopening of prosecution by filing a reply under §1.111 with or without amendment or submission of affidavits/evidence relevant to the new ground (treated as request to withdraw the appeal), or (2) maintain the appeal by filing a reply brief under §41.41 addressing each new ground as set forth in §41.37(c)(1)(vii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A reply brief to maintain appeal may not be accompanied by any amendment, affidavit (§§1.130,1.131,1.132) or other evidence; if it is, it will be treated as a request to reopen prosecution. Any amendment or affidavits/evidence must be relevant to the new ground of rejection for reopening prosecution. Extensions of time under §1.136(a) for patent applications are not applicable to this two-month period (see §1.136(b) and §1.550(c)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner’s handling of reply briefs and supplemental answers
rubrics_metrics.description: Where appellant files a timely reply brief to an examiner’s answer or a supplemental examiner’s answer, the examiner may (A) acknowledge receipt and entry of the reply brief, (B) reopen prosecution to respond to the reply brief, or (C) furnish a supplemental examiner’s answer responding to any new issue raised in the reply brief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A supplemental examiner’s answer responding to a reply brief may not include a new ground of rejection. A supplemental examiner’s answer, other than to respond to any new issue raised in the reply brief, is not permitted unless the reexamination proceeding has been remanded by the Board for such purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oral hearing request and requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If appellant desires an oral hearing, appellant must file a written request for such hearing accompanied by the fee set forth in 37 CFR 41.20(b)(3) within 2 months after the date of the examiner’s answer or supplemental examiner’s answer. The time for requesting an oral hearing may not be extended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No appellant will be permitted to participate in an oral hearing unless he or she has requested an oral hearing and submitted the fee. In reexamination proceedings, oral hearings are open to the public as observers unless appellant petitions under 37 CFR 41.3 to close the hearing, presents sufficient reasons, pays petition fee in 41.20(a), and the petition is granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty of disclosure — information material to patentability (37 CFR 1.555)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each individual associated with the patent owner in a reexamination proceeding has a duty of candor and good faith to disclose to the Office all information known to that individual to be material to patentability in the reexamination proceeding. Duty applies to patent owner, each attorney/agent representing the owner, and every other individual substantively involved on behalf of the patent owner, and continues with respect to each claim pending until cancelled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information is material when it is not cumulative and (1) it is a patent or printed publication that establishes, by itself or in combination, a prima facie case of unpatentability of a claim; or (2) it refutes or is inconsistent with a position the patent owner takes in opposing an unpatentability argument or asserting patentability. Prima facie defined as compelling conclusion of unpatentability under preponderance standard using broadest reasonable construction. IDS should be filed (preferably via 37 CFR 1.98) within two months of order for reexamination or as soon thereafter as possible. An IDS filed as a separate paper must be limited to listing the information disclosed and explanation of relevance; discussion of patentability in a separate IDS is improper (discussion may be included if filed as part of 1.530 statement). Responsibility for compliance rests on the designated individuals; Office will not evaluate compliance in the proceeding. Fraud or intentional misconduct results in noncompliance. Such issues raised during proceeding will be noted as unresolved under 1.552(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: How individuals may satisfy the disclosure duty
rubrics_metrics.description: Any individual substantively involved may satisfy the duty by disclosing the information to the attorney/agent responsible for the reexamination or to a patent owner acting in his/her own behalf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An attorney, agent, or patent owner who receives information has no duty to submit it if it is not material to patentability in the reexamination proceeding. Failure to comply risks diminishing the quality and reliability of the reexamination certificate; see MPEP §§2282 and 2686 for duty to disclose prior or concurrent proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews in ex parte reexamination — location, timing, and participants
rubrics_metrics.description: Interviews between examiners and owners (or their attorneys/agents of record) must be conducted in the Office during Office hours at times designated by the examiner; interviews will not be permitted elsewhere without Director authority. Requests that reexamination requesters participate will not be granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interviews for discussion of patentability of claims will not be conducted prior to the first official action (except where examiner initiates an interview to provide an amendment making claims patentable and the patent owner's role is passive—limited to agreeing). Interviews should be arranged in advance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written statement requirement for interviews
rubrics_metrics.description: In every instance of an interview with an examiner in an ex parte reexamination proceeding, a complete written statement of the reasons presented at the interview as warranting favorable action must be filed by the patent owner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An interview does not remove the necessity for response to Office actions specified in §1.111. The written statement must be filed as a separate part of a response to an outstanding Office action or as a separate paper within one month from the date of the interview, whichever is later. Patent owner's procedural questions may be answered by the examiner at any time during the proceeding.
